moduleTitle: Programming Languages Hub: Systems, Enterprise & Modern Languages
title: C & Memory Fundamentals: Types, Pointers & Stack vs Heap
plainExplanation: C is the foundational language underneath Linux, Windows, Python, and databases. Unlike Python which hides memory addresses from you, C lets you look directly at numbered mailboxes in RAM using Pointers — variables that store the memory address of another variable.
whyItMatters: Even if you write Python or JavaScript daily, understanding C's stack vs heap memory explains why programs crash, how garbage collectors work, and how high-performance systems stay fast.
learningObjectives: Understand static typing and why C must compile to machine code before running
Explain what a pointer holds (a memory address) and how dereferencing accesses the value
Contrast fast automatic Stack memory with flexible dynamic Heap memory
commonMistakes: Forgetting to free heap memory allocated with malloc(), causing memory leaks
Reading past the end of an array (buffer overflow), which causes crashes and security holes

questions.prompt: What does a pointer variable store in C?
options: The memory address where another value lives in RAM
Only text strings
A webpage URL
The name of the source code file
questions.correctAnswer: The memory address where another value lives in RAM
questions.explanation: A pointer holds a numeric RAM address (like 0x7ffe...), allowing direct efficient access to data without copying it.

questions.prompt: What happens if a C program repeatedly allocates Heap memory with malloc() and never calls free()?
options: A memory leak occurs, gradually consuming available RAM
The program becomes faster
The CPU automatically compresses the memory to zero bytes
Nothing — C has an automatic garbage collector
questions.correctAnswer: A memory leak occurs, gradually consuming available RAM
questions.explanation: C uses manual memory management on the heap; unfreed allocations remain occupied until the process exits.

codingChallenge.title: Simulate a Bounded Memory Buffer
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `safeWrite(bufferSize, index, value)` that prevents buffer overflows. If `index >= 0 && index < bufferSize`, return `'OK:' + index + '=' + value`. Otherwise return `'SEGFAULT'`.

visibleTests.description: Index equal to size is out of bounds

codingChallenge.solutionHint: Check `if (index >= 0 && index < bufferSize) return 'OK:' + index + '=' + value;`.

moduleTitle: Programming Languages Hub: Systems, Enterprise & Modern Languages
title: Java & Object-Oriented Programming: Classes, Encapsulation & Interfaces
plainExplanation: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) organizes code around real-world blueprints called Classes. A Class like `BankAccount` defines both the data (balance) and the safe actions (deposit, withdraw) that work on it. Encapsulation locks the balance so outside code cannot set balance = -1,000,000 directly.
whyItMatters: Java powers banking backends, Android apps, and large enterprise systems. Mastering classes, encapsulation, and interfaces transfers cleanly to C#, TypeScript, Kotlin, and Python.
learningObjectives: Explain the difference between a Class (blueprint) and an Object (living instance)
Protect internal state using encapsulation (private fields + validated methods)
Design flexible software contracts using Interfaces instead of rigid inheritance
commonMistakes: Making every field public, which lets any code corrupt internal invariants
Building deep 6-level inheritance chains instead of composing small interfaces

resources.title: University of Helsinki: Java Programming MOOC

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of Encapsulation in Object-Oriented Programming?
options: Hiding internal state and enforcing validation rules through controlled methods
Deleting all variables from memory
Making code run without a compiler
Allowing any file to overwrite private data
questions.correctAnswer: Hiding internal state and enforcing validation rules through controlled methods
questions.explanation: Encapsulation ensures invariants (like a bank balance never going below zero) are enforced in one place.

questions.prompt: How is a Class related to an Object?
options: A Class is the blueprint; an Object is a concrete instance created from that blueprint
An Object is the blueprint; a Class is the copy
They are unrelated concepts
Classes only exist in HTML
questions.correctAnswer: A Class is the blueprint; an Object is a concrete instance created from that blueprint
questions.explanation: Just as one house blueprint can build 50 distinct houses, one Class can instantiate many independent Objects.

codingChallenge.title: Encapsulated Wallet Transactions
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `processWallet(initialBalance, transactions)` where each transaction is `{ type: 'deposit' | 'withdraw', amount: number }`. Ignore invalid amounts (<= 0) and ignore withdrawals that exceed the current balance. Return the final balance.
codingChallenge.solutionHint: Check `tx.amount > 0` first. For `'deposit'`, add `tx.amount`. For `'withdraw'`, subtract only if `tx.amount <= balance`.

moduleTitle: Programming Languages Hub: Systems, Enterprise & Modern Languages
title: Modern Backend & Systems Languages: Go Concurrency & Rust Safety
plainExplanation: Modern cloud software needs speed AND safety. Go (created at Google) makes handling thousands of simultaneous network requests simple with lightweight Goroutines and Channels (like passing notes through a pipe). Rust achieves C-level speed without memory leaks or crashes using Ownership rules checked at compile time.
whyItMatters: Docker, Kubernetes, high-throughput APIs, and modern developer tools (like ripgrep and SWC) are built in Go and Rust. Learning their core mental models prepares you for senior systems and cloud engineering.
learningObjectives: Understand concurrency vs parallelism and message passing via channels in Go
Explain Rust's Ownership & Borrowing rules in plain English
Choose the right language for a project (Python vs JS/TS vs Go vs Rust)
commonMistakes: Assuming concurrency means running on multiple CPU cores simultaneously (concurrency is structure; parallelism is simultaneous execution)
Sharing mutable state across threads without locks or channels, causing race conditions

resources.title: A Tour of Go (Interactive Official Guide)

questions.prompt: What problem does Rust's Ownership model solve at compile time?
options: Prevents memory leaks, use-after-free bugs, and data races without needing a runtime garbage collector
Automatically designs CSS layouts
Eliminates the need for HTTP
Replaces SQL databases
questions.correctAnswer: Prevents memory leaks, use-after-free bugs, and data races without needing a runtime garbage collector
questions.explanation: By tracking exactly which variable owns each piece of memory at compile time, Rust frees memory deterministically and prevents dangling pointers.

questions.prompt: What is Go's core proverb about safe concurrency?
options: Do not communicate by sharing memory; instead, share memory by communicating (using channels)
Always use global variables for every goroutine
Never handle errors
Run only one function per computer
questions.correctAnswer: Do not communicate by sharing memory; instead, share memory by communicating (using channels)
questions.explanation: Passing data through channels ensures only one goroutine owns the value at a time, avoiding subtle race conditions.

codingChallenge.title: Simulate a Bounded Worker Queue
codingChallenge.instructions: Write a JavaScript function `batchJobs(jobs, workerCount)` that splits an array of job names into `workerCount` round-robin worker buckets (arrays). Example: `batchJobs(['a','b','c'], 2)` -> `[['a','c'], ['b']]`.

hiddenTests.description: Creates all worker buckets even if some are empty

codingChallenge.solutionHint: Initialize `buckets = Array.from({ length: workerCount }, () => [])`, then push `jobs[i]` into `buckets[i % workerCount]`.
